I will keep it simple and steady this year. In Quzhou County, the crop pattern I trust most is winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land. At 61, I would rather run a familiar system with stable yields and manageable labor than chase a riskier cash crop. I will use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed, put most of my fertilizer into the staple grains, irrigate only at the key stages, and keep pesticide use to the minimum needed to protect yield. I will plough before wheat to set up a good seedbed, then use rotary tillage after wheat harvest so I can plant maize quickly. I am assuming I have 20 mu of land, and I will double-crop all of it because that gives me grain for security, straw for use, and the best fit for my climate, water conditions, and work capacity.
